questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which choice best defines active listening?

answer.text: A. Listening with attention, checking meaning, and responding thoughtfully

feedback.text: Correct. Active listening includes focus, understanding, and a useful response.

answer.text: B. Staying silent no matter what happens

feedback.text: Silence can be respectful, but active listening also requires understanding and response when appropriate.

answer.text: C. Planning your own answer while someone else talks

feedback.text: This divides attention. Active listening begins with understanding the speaker's message.

answer.text: D. Agreeing with every idea

feedback.text: Active listening does not require agreement. It requires respectful attention and response.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

In a planning discussion, a speaker says, "We need a stronger closing." Which response best supports collaboration?

answer.text: A. No, that is not important.

feedback.text: This shuts down the idea without listening or giving a reason.

answer.text: B. I do not want to talk about the closing.

feedback.text: This avoids the group's shared task.

answer.text: C. What kind of closing do you think would help the audience remember our point?

feedback.text: Correct. This question listens to the idea and invites the speaker to develop it.

answer.text: D. I already did enough work.

feedback.text: This centers the listener's frustration rather than the group's goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response focuses on the idea instead of attacking the person?

answer.text: A. You always make confusing suggestions.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and uses an absolute claim instead of addressing the idea.

answer.text: B. I am not sure the example fits our topic because it does not connect to the main point.

feedback.text: Correct. This response gives a reason about the idea and keeps the discussion respectful.

answer.text: C. That is a terrible idea because you said it.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and does not explain a communication concern.

answer.text: D. Nobody should listen to you.

feedback.text: This is disrespectful and blocks collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A group member has not spoken during planning. What is the best collaborative move?

answer.text: A. Ignore the person because quiet people have no ideas.

feedback.text: This assumption is unfair and prevents full group participation.

answer.text: B. Tell the person they are ruining the group.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and does not invite communication.

answer.text: C. Finish the plan without them.

feedback.text: This may exclude a useful perspective.

answer.text: D. Ask, "What do you think would help our audience understand the topic?"

feedback.text: Correct. This invites participation and connects the question to the group's communication goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which phrase is most appropriate for academic communication in a speech planning meeting?

answer.text: A. Your part is weird.

feedback.text: This is vague and personal. Academic communication should be specific and respectful.

answer.text: B. Your section has useful evidence, but it needs a clearer connection to the main idea.

feedback.text: Correct. This response uses precise language and gives actionable feedback.

answer.text: C. I hate this topic.

feedback.text: This expresses emotion but does not help the group improve the speech.

answer.text: D. Just make it sound better somehow.

feedback.text: This is too vague to guide revision.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which behavior would most likely harm a collaborative discussion?

answer.text: A. Interrupting each speaker before they finish

feedback.text: Correct. Interrupting prevents full listening and can stop useful ideas from being shared.

answer.text: B. Asking a clarifying question

feedback.text: Clarifying questions support understanding and collaboration.

answer.text: C. Paraphrasing a group member's idea

feedback.text: Paraphrasing shows active listening and helps check meaning.

answer.text: D. Inviting a quiet member to share

feedback.text: Inviting participation supports collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best helps a classmate understand instructions?

answer.text: A. I am not explaining it.

feedback.text: This refuses to support communication.

answer.text: B. You should guess what the teacher means.

feedback.text: Guessing can lead to incorrect work. Instructional communication should clarify expectations.

answer.text: C. The directions say to post one claim and one reason; start with your claim first.

feedback.text: Correct. This points to the task and breaks it into a first step.

answer.text: D. Write more words so it looks finished.

feedback.text: This focuses on length, not understanding the assignment.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

What should a listener do before disagreeing with a speaker?

answer.text: A. Decide the speaker is wrong immediately.

feedback.text: This skips understanding and can lead to unfair disagreement.

answer.text: B. Change the topic quickly.

feedback.text: Changing the topic avoids the speaker's idea.

answer.text: C. Repeat the same disagreement louder.

feedback.text: Volume does not improve reasoning or listening.

answer.text: D. Make sure they understand the speaker's point.

feedback.text: Correct. Understanding the idea first helps the listener disagree respectfully and accurately.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best builds on another person's idea?

answer.text: A. Your point about audience attention connects to our opening; we could add a question there.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects the idea to the speech plan and adds a useful next step.

answer.text: B. I do not remember what you said.

feedback.text: This does not build on the idea because it does not show understanding.

answer.text: C. Stop talking about the audience.

feedback.text: This shuts down the topic instead of developing it.

answer.text: D. That has nothing to do with me.

feedback.text: This avoids the shared group task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which statement best explains why collaboration matters in speech communication?

answer.text: A. It lets one person control all decisions.

feedback.text: This is the opposite of collaboration. Collaboration shares responsibility.

answer.text: B. It helps group members combine ideas, solve problems, and improve the final message.

feedback.text: Correct. Collaboration improves communication by using multiple perspectives toward a shared goal.

answer.text: C. It removes the need to listen.

feedback.text: Collaboration requires listening because group members must understand each other.

answer.text: D. It means every idea must be used.

feedback.text: Collaboration considers ideas, but not every idea has to be included.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response is a respectful disagreement?

answer.text: A. That idea is stupid.

feedback.text: This attacks the idea in a disrespectful way and gives no reason.

answer.text: B. You never help us.

feedback.text: This attacks the person and uses an absolute claim.

answer.text: C. I see the goal, but I think a shorter example would keep the audience focused.

feedback.text: Correct. This acknowledges the idea, gives a reason, and stays connected to the speech goal.

answer.text: D. I refuse to discuss it.

feedback.text: This stops the discussion rather than disagreeing constructively.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which choice uses the clearest academic language?

answer.text: A. The evidence supports our point, but we need to explain how it connects to the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses precise communication words and gives a clear revision need.

answer.text: B. The stuff is kind of there.

feedback.text: This is vague. It does not identify what needs to improve.

answer.text: C. It is fine or whatever.

feedback.text: This is informal and does not provide useful communication feedback.

answer.text: D. Make the thing better.

feedback.text: This is too general to guide improvement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A speaker says, "I am not sure our order makes sense." What is the best active listening response?

answer.text: A. The order is fine because I said so.

feedback.text: This dismisses the concern and gives no evidence.

answer.text: B. We do not have time for your concern.

feedback.text: This shuts down the speaker rather than addressing the message.

answer.text: C. I was not listening.

feedback.text: This directly shows a lack of active listening.

answer.text: D. You are concerned about organization. Which part feels out of order?

feedback.text: Correct. This paraphrases the concern and asks a clarifying question.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which choice is an example of turn-taking in discussion?

answer.text: A. Speaking over others until they stop

feedback.text: This prevents others from completing their thoughts.

answer.text: B. Waiting for a speaker to finish, then responding to the idea

feedback.text: Correct. This respects the speaker's turn and keeps the response connected to the discussion.

answer.text: C. Ignoring the topic and starting a new one

feedback.text: This breaks the flow of discussion.

answer.text: D. Letting only the loudest person decide

feedback.text: This does not support equal participation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

In a school setting, which response best supports social communication?

answer.text: A. Move, I need that seat.

feedback.text: This is abrupt and does not show respectful social communication.

answer.text: B. I do not care what anyone needs.

feedback.text: This blocks cooperation.

answer.text: C. Could we make space so everyone in the group can see the notes?

feedback.text: Correct. This politely identifies a shared need and supports group participation.

answer.text: D. Nobody else should talk.

feedback.text: This prevents communication and participation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which question best clarifies a speaker's message?

answer.text: A. Why are you always confusing?

feedback.text: This attacks the speaker instead of clarifying the message.

answer.text: B. Can you explain what you mean by "stronger evidence"?

feedback.text: Correct. This asks for the meaning of a specific phrase and helps the listener understand.

answer.text: C. Can we stop listening now?

feedback.text: This stops communication instead of clarifying it.

answer.text: D. Do you even know the topic?

feedback.text: This challenges the person in a disrespectful way.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which choice best shows that a listener has understood a speaker?

answer.text: A. The listener paraphrases the main idea accurately.

feedback.text: Correct. Accurate paraphrasing shows that the listener received and understood the message.

answer.text: B. The listener looks away and changes the topic.

feedback.text: This suggests the listener may not be focused on the message.

answer.text: C. The listener repeats one random word.

feedback.text: Repeating a word does not prove the listener understood the main idea.

answer.text: D. The listener disagrees before the speaker finishes.

feedback.text: This prevents full understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best helps solve a group disagreement?

answer.text: A. I win because I talked first.

feedback.text: This is about control, not collaboration.

answer.text: B. The loudest person should choose.

feedback.text: Volume is not a good reason for a decision.

answer.text: C. We should stop working together.

feedback.text: This avoids solving the disagreement.

answer.text: D. Let's list both options and decide which one better supports our audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a fair process and connects the decision to the communication goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which response best uses academic vocabulary during feedback?

answer.text: A. It sounds bad.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not identify the communication issue.

answer.text: B. I do not like it.

feedback.text: This is an opinion without useful explanation.

answer.text: C. Your organization is clear, but the transition between points needs to be smoother.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses communication vocabulary and gives specific feedback.

answer.text: D. Just talk nicer.

feedback.text: This is too general to guide improvement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A group member says, "I think our example is too long." Which reply is most collaborative?

answer.text: A. You are just trying to do less work.

feedback.text: This attacks motive instead of addressing the idea.

answer.text: B. I do not care about length.

feedback.text: This ignores the concern.

answer.text: C. Long examples are always better.

feedback.text: This uses an absolute claim without considering the audience.

answer.text: D. Let's check whether the example supports the main point or could be shortened.

feedback.text: Correct. This addresses the concern and suggests a useful next step.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

What is the main purpose of a respectful response?

answer.text: A. To address the idea in a way that keeps communication productive

feedback.text: Correct. Respectful responses focus on ideas and help the discussion continue.

answer.text: B. To avoid all disagreement

feedback.text: Respectful communication can include disagreement when it is handled with reasons and care.

answer.text: C. To make the other person stop talking

feedback.text: This blocks communication rather than supporting it.

answer.text: D. To prove the listener is smarter

feedback.text: This focuses on status, not shared understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best supports a peer who missed a direction?

answer.text: A. You missed it, so that is your problem.

feedback.text: This is not supportive social or instructional communication.

answer.text: B. The direction was to submit one paragraph. I can show you where it says that.

feedback.text: Correct. This clarifies the task and helps the peer locate the instruction.

answer.text: C. Just submit nothing.

feedback.text: This does not help the peer complete the task.

answer.text: D. Ask someone else because I refuse.

feedback.text: This refuses communication support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best shows a listener connecting ideas?

answer.text: A. I forgot what everyone said.

feedback.text: This does not connect ideas.

answer.text: B. Your idea has no connection to anything.

feedback.text: This dismisses the idea without analysis.

answer.text: C. Your point about practice connects to Mia's concern about sounding prepared.

feedback.text: Correct. This links two group members' ideas and helps the discussion become more organized.

answer.text: D. Let us stop planning.

feedback.text: This ends the discussion instead of connecting ideas.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which choice is the best sign of collaborative communication?

answer.text: A. One person makes every decision alone.

feedback.text: This removes shared responsibility.

answer.text: B. Group members compete to speak the longest.

feedback.text: This focuses on control, not collaboration.

answer.text: C. Group members ignore questions.

feedback.text: Ignoring questions blocks understanding.

answer.text: D. Group members listen, respond, and build a shared plan.

feedback.text: Correct. Collaboration requires listening, responding, and working toward a common goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best repairs a misunderstanding?

answer.text: A. I may have misunderstood. Did you mean that the introduction needs a clearer hook?

feedback.text: Correct. This admits possible misunderstanding and asks a specific clarifying question.

answer.text: B. You said it wrong, so it is your fault.

feedback.text: This blames the speaker and does not repair understanding.

answer.text: C. I will pretend I understood.

feedback.text: Pretending does not solve the communication problem.

answer.text: D. Your point does not matter.

feedback.text: This dismisses the message instead of repairing the misunderstanding.
